runs.summary: 3 new podcast recommendations for week of 2026-10-22 (In Good Company, ChinaTalk, The Lazarus Heist)
runs.content:
## Week of 2026-10-22

### In Good Company with Nicolai Tangen
Host: Nicolai Tangen (CEO, Norges Bank Investment Management; ex-AKO Capital)
Why for Fred: Tangen, a former European hedge-fund founder, interviews the CEOs of the companies Norway's sovereign fund owns (Aviva, Orange, Arista), plus macro and geopolitics figures (Georgieva, Stoltenberg). It's a European-investor take on management quality, next to Behind the Balance Sheet.
Format: Weekly long-form CEO interview (~45-60 min) + Friday highlights
Start with: Michael Bloomberg (2026), or Amanda Blanc on the Aviva turnaround
Links: https://www.nbim.no/en/news-and-insights/podcast/

### ChinaTalk
Host: Jordan Schneider
Why for Fred: Where AI meets geopolitics: chips, export controls, GPU smuggling, China's AI labs. It's the policy layer under the Dwarkesh compute-economics episodes and the world-order themes from the Prof. Jiang episode. Guests are specialists, not pundits.
Format: Long-form interview/panel, several a week, ~45-90 min
Start with: "GPU Smuggling, OpenAI Cooked?" with Nathan Lambert (Mar 2026)
Links: https://www.chinatalk.media

### The Lazarus Heist (BBC World Service)
Hosts: Geoff White, Jean Lee
Why for Fred: The natural next listen after CyberHack: The Conti Files and Where Is Austin Tice?. A serialised BBC investigation of North Korea's state hackers, from the $1bn Bangladesh Bank attempt to crypto-exchange thefts. Peabody-nominated, and it links to his DeFi interest.
Format: Serialised documentary, multiple seasons, ~30 min episodes
Start with: Season 1, Episode 1
Links: BBC Sounds

runs.summary: 4 new podcast recommendations for week of 2026-10-17 (The Business Brew, Unsupervised Learning, Live Long and Master Aging, Bell Curve)
runs.content:
## Week of 2026-10-17

### The Business Brew
Host: Bill Brewster (long-time value investor, ex-Sullimar Capital)
Why for Fred: Brewster runs long, unhurried conversations about capital allocation and the psychology of investing with PMs, sell-side analysts and owner-operators. It's a natural sibling to behind the balance sheet and pender fund. Previous value suggestions (Acquirers, Yet Another Value, Value Investing with Legends) are mostly about single stock pitches. Business Brew spends more time on how investors think: position sizing, beauty-contest dynamics, and when to revisit a thesis. That fits Fred's Berkshire/MOI-style principles.
Format: Long-form interview, roughly fortnightly, ~60–120 min
Sample episode to start with: "Revisiting Fairfax Financial" with Charles Frischer and Asheef Lalani (Apr 30, 2026), a Berkshire-style insurance compounder case study. Or "Notes From The Beauty Contest" (Mar 21, 2026).
Links: Pocket Casts (https://pocketcasts.com/podcast/the-business-brew/ccaeae70-0c03-0139-41b8-0acc26574db2) · Pod Engine (https://www.podengine.ai/podcasts/the-business-brew)

---

### Unsupervised Learning with Jacob Effron
Host: Jacob Effron (Redpoint Ventures), with Patrick Chase, Jordan Segall and Erica Brescia
Why for Fred: Fred follows the dwarkesh compute prices 10x inference-economics angle and enterprise adoption (me myself and ai bank of america bernard hampton). Unsupervised Learning sits between those two. It's a VC asking researchers and AI-company CEOs what actually works in production and where the margins are. He has also interviewed Benedict Evans (Fred liked him on lennys podcast benedict evans episode). It's more investor-minded than Interconnects and less hype-driven than No Priors.
Format: Long-form interview, roughly every 2–4 weeks, ~45–70 min
Sample episode to start with: Ep 94: "Applied Compute CEO on the Limits of RL, the New AI Hyperscaler & Why Post-Training Wins Inference" (Oct 6, 2026). Or the Benedict Evans episode (Ep 91, Jul 2026).
Links: Apple Podcasts (https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/unsupervised-learning-with-jacob-effron/id1672188924)

---

### Live Long and Master Aging (Live Long with Peter Bowes)
Host: Peter Bowes (former BBC Los Angeles correspondent, HealthSpan Media)
Why for Fred: Bowes is a fifty-something journalist who runs the same longevity experiment on himself (fasting, endurance, sleep). He interviews both researchers and midlife "ordinary" people who changed course. The show focuses on healthspan in midlife, which matches Fred's longevity-for-men-at-50 interest. It's also more journalistic and sceptical than the clinician-led shows already suggested (Attia, FoundMyFitness, The Proof). Episodes are shorter, which makes them easy to slot between Diary of a CEO marathons.
Format: Long-form one-to-one interview, weekly, ~30–50 min
Sample episode to start with: Jeffrey Weiss on what's still possible in midlife: first 10K at 48, then Ironman twice (Jun 19, 2026). Or Paul Irving (Milken Institute) on the "longevity dividend".
Links: livelongpodcast.com (https://livelongpodcast.com) · Apple Podcasts (https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/live-long-and-master-aging/id1211124529)

---

### Bell Curve (Blockworks)
Hosts: Mike Ippolito, Jason Yanowitz, with Myles and Xavier on Roundups
Why for Fred: Fred's crypto interest is DeFi protocols rather than price talk. Bell Curve runs thesis-driven seasons (its first was a DeFi credit thesis) plus roundups on curator models, counterparty risk and exploit security. It's more analytical than Unchained or The Chopping Block, both already suggested. It also pairs well with Fred's live crypto holdings (LINK etc.) by covering the fundamental protocol-revenue debate.
Format: Thesis-driven seasons plus weekly roundups, ~45–75 min
Sample episode to start with: "What Brings Capital Back to DeFi?" (Roundup, mid-2026), or "The Bull & Bear Cases For Ethereum"
Links: blockworks.co/podcast/bellcurve (https://blockworks.co/podcast/bellcurve) · Apple Podcasts (https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/bell-curve/id1641356619)
